title: Adding EasyEnsemble as a third candidate in the SRDF pool

motivation.evidence: In the S05 conditional view (375 triggered cases), EasyEnsemble achieved balanced accuracy 0.8684, the highest among all baselines and significantly above SRDF v1 (0.7919). SRDF v1/v2/v3 used only {GradientBoosting, SMOTE_RandomForest}. The Arbiter had no opportunity to select EasyEnsemble.

hypothesis: Adding EasyEnsemble to the SRDF candidate pool will increase the framework-level mean delta on the 600 triggered cases above v3, because the Arbiter will select EasyEnsemble on cases where it outperforms the existing candidates.

software_changes.generator_change: Add a third candidate dict: {'name': 'EasyEnsemble', 'graph': ['Input','EasyEnsemble','Output'], 'resource_cost': 2.0, 'description': 'EasyEnsemble balanced bagging.'}
software_changes.core_change: In _evaluate_candidate, add branch for 'EasyEnsemble' using imblearn.ensemble.EasyEnsembleClassifier(n_estimators=10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=-1).

H1.claim: v4 framework mean > v3 framework mean on 600 triggered cases.
H1.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank on dataset-level deltas (v4 - v3), two-sided.

H2.claim: v4 framework mean is within 0.005 of standalone EasyEnsemble on the same 600 triggered cases.

H3.claim: The Arbiter selects EasyEnsemble on at least 30% of SUCCESS cases.
H3.test: Selection frequency of 'EasyEnsemble' among v4 SUCCESS cases.

cohort: Same as S06a/S06b (stage_198, 600 triggered cases, 24 datasets)
metric: Balanced accuracy on held-out test fold

stopping_rules.null_finding: Any failed hypothesis is documented; no re-run with different parameters.

expected_outcomes.optimistic: v4 adds +1 to +2 pp over v3.
